   crosshair points at), `looking-at`, `entities [RADIUS] [TYPE]` (mobs with
   ids and health, dropped items, orbs), `block X Y Z`, `blocks X1 Y1 Z1 X2 Y2 Z2`, `light X1 Y1 Z1 X2 Y2 Z2`,
   `find-block BLOCK [RADIUS]`, `inventory` (stacks with their components as
   SNBT), `screen` (the open screen or title menu, its buttons and slots) and
   `messages` (chat, title, subtitle and action bar).
 - **Move and act:** `move DIR SECONDS`, `jump`, `goto X Y Z` (A* over standable
   blocks: steps up one block, drops up to three, avoids lava), `look`,
   `look-at` a point, block face or entity, `attack [ID]`, `break X Y Z`,
   `place X Y Z [--item ITEM]`, `interact X Y Z` (doors, chests, crafting
   tables), `use-item [--hold S]` (eat, drink, throw), `select SLOT|ITEM`, `drop`.
 - **Widgets:** `ui` lists every widget of the open screen (title menus, pause,
   options pages, inventories and menus): an id, its kind
   (`button`, `slider` with its 0..1 `value`, `field`, `row`, `tab` with
   `selected`, `slot` with its stack), the label and its bounds. Ids come from
   labels (`FOV: 70` is `fov`, `Video Settings...` is `video-settings`, a
   world row is the world's name; a repeat gets `-2`), else `row-0`, `field-0`,
   and slots are `slot-ID`. `click ID [right] [shift]` clicks one as the mouse
   would and `set ID VALUE` moves a slider to 0..1; after a click, the next
   `ui`, `click` or `set` waits for the screen to be redrawn. Design and plans:
   [agent-control.md](agent-control.md).
 - **Options:** `options-get [KEY...]` gives every `options.txt` option by its
   vanilla key with its value and what it accepts (`{"type": "int", "min": 30,
   "max": 110, "value": 70}`; enums with `choices`, key bindings as
   `key.keyboard.w`); `options-set KEY VALUE` sets one, applies it at once and
   saves `options.txt` as the options screen does. A value the option refuses
   is an error saying what it accepts, not vanilla's silent reset.
 - **Waits and events:** `wait-for screen NAME|widget ID|loaded|chat TEXT|event
   KIND [--timeout S] [--since SEQ]` replies o

I'm thinking about how to handle clipboard operations. If the clipboard is empty or contains no text, then I should ensure it doesn't get copied.  # Horizon Android Vulkan render check
 
 This is the first Android build milestone for Horizon: a small ARM64 NativeActivity APK that drives winit 0.30.13 and wgpu 30.0.1 through Android's Vulkan surface lifecycle and presents a visible diagnostic frame.
 
 **This is not the Horizon game client.** The smoke APK does not load a world, use the existing `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`, or bundle Minecraft files. It leaves the desktop renderer and PojavLauncher unchanged. No Minecraft resources are needed for this test.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 - Android starts `android.app.NativeActivity` from `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`; its library name is `horizon_android`.
 - `android/native` builds `libhorizon_android.so` as a Rust `cdylib`. `android_main(AndroidApp)` initializes Android logging and starts the render check.
 - winit receives the `AndroidApp` through `EventLoopBuilderExtAndroid::with_android_app`. Its resumed/suspended/window events create and release the probe surface/renderer.
 - wgpu is restricted to Vulkan for this diagnostic. The app logs the adapter, driver, surface format/size, lifecycle, and `PRESENTED_FRAME` after the queue submits and presents a frame.
 - The diagnostic uses the same pinned winit and wgpu versions as Horizon. It is intentionally separate from `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`.
 
 ## Build the debug APK on Linux x86-64
 
 Toolchain baseline: Rust 1.95.0, JDK 17, Gradle 8.13, Android Gradle Plugin 8.7.2, SDK Platform/Build Tools 35, and NDK 27.2.12479018. Rust 1.95.0 is required by the current Horizon workspace (`horizon-mods`); it is newer than the standalone probe's original Rust baseline.
 
 Install the Android Rust target once:
 
 ```sh
 rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --profile minimal
 rustup target add aarch64-linux-android --toolchain 1.95.0
 ```
 
 Set the Android/JDK environment and build:
 
 ```sh
 export JAVA_HOME="$HOME/.local/jdks/temurin-17.0.13+11"
 export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android/Sdk"
 export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_HOME"
 export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/27.2.12479018"
 export ANDROID_NDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_NDK_HOME"
 export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
 
 sdkmanager --licenses
 sdkmanager --install "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "ndk;27.2.12479018"
 
 cd horizon/android
 ./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace :app:assembleDebug
 ```
 
 Gradle runs the pinned Rust toolchain for `aarch64-linux-android`, uses the NDK's API-26 linker, and copies the shared library into generated build output before packaging. The APK is:
 
 ```text
 horizon/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
 ```
 
 ## Install and test on a physical Android device (Windows PowerShell)
 
 Use an arm64 device with Android API 26+ and Vulkan 1.0 support. From the repository root, install and launch:
 
 ```powershell
 $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
 $apk = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\android\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk).Path
 adb devices -l
 adb install -r $apk
 adb shell am force-stop dev.playhorizon.horizon
 adb logcat -c
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon/android.app.NativeActivity
 Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
 adb logcat -d -v threadtime -s HorizonAndroid:I AndroidRuntime:E |
     Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-render.log
 @(
     "manufacturer=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer)"
     "model=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.model)"
     "android=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.release)"
     "api=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.sdk)"
     "abi=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abi)"
 ) | Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-device.txt
 adb shell screencap -p /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png
 adb pull /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png .\horizon-android-render.png
 ```
 
 A successful device render must show the non-black diagnostic frame and matching `PRESENTED_FRAME` evidence identifying the Vulkan backend, adapter, dimensions, and format. The APK build and a successful Activity launch alone do not prove presentation. Preserve the device model/API/ABI, GPU/driver, full relevant log, and screenshot or video when reporting the result.
 
 The APK output above is separate from `/workspaces/horizon-android/app-debug.apk`, the already-tested standalone probe APK; this build does not overwrite that file.
 
 ## Known blockers and next milestone
 
 - The existing `horizon-client` crate is not currently an Android build target. An Android-target check while testing direct linkage failed in `arboard 3.6.1`: that dependency selects no clipboard implementation for Android. Do not paper over this by silently disabling clipboard behavior. A deliberate Android clipboard backend or a scoped platform abstraction is needed before wiring the full client.
 - The smoke APK does not import Minecraft resources or enter a world. A later client milestone must define a user-owned resource import into app-private storage, adapt filesystem/audio/input assumptions, then validate the real game renderer and local-world entry on hardware.
 - Physical-device testing of this Horizon APK is still outstanding. The separate standalone probe's successful Xiaomi Redmi Note 13 run does not count as evidence for this APK.

 /// The loading screen's renderer: the real HUD atlas and font over one opaque
 /// white block-sprite layer, an empty border texture and the title panorama
 /// once the menu bundle is ready.
 fn loading_renderer(
     window: Arc<Window>,
     offscreen: bool,
     gui: Option<&UiResources>,
     previous: Option<&Renderer>,
     api: horizon_client::graphics::GraphicsApi,
 ) -> Result<Renderer> {
     static FORCEFIELD: [u8; 4] = [0; 4];
     static EMPTY_HUD: [u8; 4] = [0, 0, 0, 255];
     static EMPTY_GLINT: [u8; 4] = [0; 4];
     let empty_panorama = horizon_client::gfx::panorama::Faces {
         size: 1,
         pixels: [0u8; 4].repeat(6),
     };
     let panorama = gui.map_or(&empty_panorama, |gui| gui.panorama.as_ref());
     let atlas = gui.map(|gui| &gui.atlas);
     let (pixels, width, height) = match atlas {
         Some(atlas) => (atlas.pixels.as_slice(), atlas.width, atlas.height),
         None => (EMPTY_HUD.as_slice(), 1, 1),
     };
     let (glint_pixels, glint_width, glint_height) = match atlas {
         Some(atlas) => (atlas.glint.0.as_slice(), atlas.glint.1, atlas.glint.2),
         None => (EMPTY_GLINT.as_slice(), 1, 1),
     };
     // A glyph rasterized into an earlier texture is not in these pixels; the
     // new texture gets it again when the character is drawn (see
     // `build_renderer`).
     if let Some(atlas) = atlas {
         atlas.font.reset_cache();
     }
     let mut renderer = pollster::block_on(Renderer::new(
         window,
         offscreen,
         &[255, 255, 255, 255],
         1,
         1,
         1,
         &[],
         &[],
         (pixels, width, height),
         (glint_pixels, glint_width, glint_height),
         (glint_pixels, glint_width, glint_height),
         (&FORCEFIELD[..], 1),
         panorama,
         None,
         previous,
         api,
     ))?;
     if let Some(atlas) = atlas {
         renderer.hud.sprite_animations = atlas
             .sprite_animations
             .iter()
             .map(|(rect, animation)| (*rect, animation.clone(), (usize::MAX, 0, 0)))
             .collect();
     }
     Ok(renderer)
 }

 # Horizon Android Vulkan render check
 
 This is the first Android build milestone for Horizon: a small ARM64 NativeActivity APK that drives winit 0.30.13 and wgpu 30.0.1 through Android's Vulkan surface lifecycle and presents a visible diagnostic frame.
 
 **This is not the Horizon game client.** The smoke APK does not load a world, use the existing `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`, or bundle Minecraft files. It leaves the desktop renderer and PojavLauncher unchanged. No Minecraft resources are needed for this test.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 - Android starts `android.app.NativeActivity` from `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`; its library name is `horizon_android`.
 - `android/native` builds `libhorizon_android.so` as a Rust `cdylib`. `android_main(AndroidApp)` initializes Android logging and starts the render check.
 - winit receives the `AndroidApp` through `EventLoopBuilderExtAndroid::with_android_app`. Its resumed/suspended/window events create and release the probe surface/renderer.
 - wgpu is restricted to Vulkan for this diagnostic. The app logs the adapter, driver, surface format/size, lifecycle, and `PRESENTED_FRAME` after the queue submits and presents a frame.
 - The diagnostic uses the same pinned winit and wgpu versions as Horizon. It is intentionally separate from `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`.
 
 ## Build the debug APK on Linux x86-64
 
 Toolchain baseline: Rust 1.95.0, JDK 17, Gradle 8.13, Android Gradle Plugin 8.7.2, SDK Platform/Build Tools 35, and NDK 27.2.12479018. Rust 1.95.0 is required by the current Horizon workspace (`horizon-mods`); it is newer than the standalone probe's original Rust baseline.
 
 Install the Android Rust target once:
 
 ```sh
 rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --profile minimal
 rustup target add aarch64-linux-android --toolchain 1.95.0
 ```
 
 Set the Android/JDK environment and build:
 
 ```sh
 export JAVA_HOME="$HOME/.local/jdks/temurin-17.0.13+11"
 export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android/Sdk"
 export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_HOME"
 export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/27.2.12479018"
 export ANDROID_NDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_NDK_HOME"
 export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
 
 sdkmanager --licenses
 sdkmanager --install "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "ndk;27.2.12479018"
 
 cd horizon/android
 ./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace :app:assembleDebug
 ```
 
 Gradle runs the pinned Rust toolchain for `aarch64-linux-android`, uses the NDK's API-26 linker, and copies the shared library into generated build output before packaging. The APK is:
 
 ```text
 horizon/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
 ```
 
 ## Install and test on a physical Android device (Windows PowerShell)
 
 Use an arm64 device with Android API 26+ and Vulkan 1.0 support. From the repository root, install and launch:
 
 ```powershell
 $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
 $apk = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\android\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk).Path
 adb devices -l
 adb install -r $apk
 adb shell am force-stop dev.playhorizon.horizon
 adb logcat -c
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon/android.app.NativeActivity
 Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
 adb logcat -d -v threadtime -s HorizonAndroid:I AndroidRuntime:E |
     Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-render.log
 @(
     "manufacturer=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer)"
     "model=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.model)"
     "android=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.release)"
     "api=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.sdk)"
     "abi=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abi)"
 ) | Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-device.txt
 adb shell screencap -p /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png
 adb pull /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png .\horizon-android-render.png
 ```
 
 A successful device render must show the non-black diagnostic frame and matching `PRESENTED_FRAME` evidence identifying the Vulkan backend, adapter, dimensions, and format. The APK build and a successful Activity launch alone do not prove presentation. Preserve the device model/API/ABI, GPU/driver, full relevant log, and screenshot or video when reporting the result.
 
 The APK output above is separate from `/workspaces/horizon-android/app-debug.apk`, the already-tested standalone probe APK; this build does not overwrite that file.

 # Horizon native client
 
 `horizon-client` is the playable Rust client for Minecraft Java Edition 26.3.
 It streams a world around the player on worker threads, renders every vanilla
 block model with smooth lighting and biome tints, and runs the validated player
 physics, health and hunger at 20 ticks per second. You can mine with vanilla
 hardness/tool rules, collect drops from the block loot tables, place blocks,
 craft in the 2x2 inventory grid or on a crafting table, and save and reload worlds
 in vanilla's Anvil format.
 
 **Status:** playable; players get it through [the launcher](../launcher/README.md). The [Java parity table](../README.md#project-status)
 in the README scores each subsystem against vanilla and lists what is still
 missing; [Rust rewrite status](rust-parity.md) has the details.
 
 ## Run from a checkout
 
 Use current stable Rust (1.90+) and JDK 25 (Python 3.10+ only for the development
 harnesses). Horizon never
 downloads the game: resource preparation imports **your own copy** (the 26.3
 client from your official launcher install, and the 26.3 server jar you
 downloaded yourself; see [Build from source](../README.md#build-from-source)),
 verifies it against the pinned checksums, runs vanilla's data generator and small
 exporters against those jars, and extracts the jar's assets and data into ignored
 `.local/horizon-client/26.3/`. Sounds (about 380 MB) are copied from your
 launcher's asset store by `horizon-prepare sounds`, each file checked against the asset
 index's SHA-1. Preparation also tries to replace the JAR's gray 1×1 title panorama
 placeholders with the full textures from that asset store. If the store is missing or
 incomplete, preparation logs a warning and keeps the placeholders. To import the panorama
 later without rerunning the Java exporters, run `horizon-prepare panorama` (or
 `cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- panorama` in a checkout). Pass
 `--minecraft-dir PATH` when using a different Minecraft installation.
 Prepared resources are private; never commit them.
 
 Preparation is `horizon-prepare` (`crates/horizon-prepare`, Rust): it needs no Python, only
 the JDK, for the small exporters that call Mojang's own code. Release folders ship it beside
 `horizon-client`, and the launcher prepares with it and copies the sounds as part of preparing.
 
 ```sh
 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar
 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds
 cargo run --release -p horizon-client -- --render-distance 12
 ```
 
 Development builds that link quickly: `cargo build --profile fast -p horizon-client`.
 
 | Option | Meaning |
 | --- | --- |
 | `--world NAME` | World folder under `saves/` (default "New World"); reopened if it exists |
 | `--seed N` | Seed for a new world (numbers or text, like vanilla) |
 | `--creative` | Creative mode (instant breaking, pick block) |
 | `--render-distance N` | Chunks, 2..64 (default 12) |
 | `--resources PATH` | Prepared resource directory |
 
 | Control | Action |
 | --- | --- |
 | Mouse | Look (vanilla default sensitivity) |
 | WASD / Space / Left Shift / Left Ctrl | Move, jump, sneak, sprint |
 | Left / right click | Break (hold) / place or use; right click opens crafting tables |
 | Middle click | Pick block (creative) |
 | 1–9, scroll | Select hotbar slot |
 | E | Inventory and 2x2 crafting (shift-click to quick-move or craft all) |
 | Q / Ctrl+Q | Drop one / drop stack |
 | F3 | Debug overlay (position, chunk, light, biome, FPS) |
 | Esc | Pause menu (Save and Quit) |
 
 Worlds autosave every 6000 ticks (5 minutes), when chunks unload and on quit.
 On headless Linux use `vscreen start ./target/release/horizon-client` and
 `vscreen shot`.
 
 Sound: the game prints the output it opened (`Horizon: audio output ...`) or
 why it has none (`Horizon: no sound: ...`). It opens none with
 `HORIZON_NO_AUDIO` set, nor on a `vscreen`, where tests run beside someone
 listening; `HORIZON_AUDIO=1` opens it there anyway, so send it to a null sink
 (`PIPEWIRE_PROPS='{ target.object=<sink> node.dont-fallback=true }'`). Don't
 mute a test run's stream in the mixer: PipeWire remembers the mute for every
 later `horizon-client`. The launcher starts the game as "Horizon" for that
 reason.
 
 ### Agent control (`horizon-ctl` and MCP)
 
 AI agents and scripts play Horizon through `horizon-ctl`, a command line that
 reads the game as JSON and acts like a player, and `horizon-ctl mcp`, an MCP
 server with the same commands. `--control` makes the game accept them on a
 local socket; under control, losing window focus does not pause the game or
 release held keys, so a script can play while you use other windows.
 
 ```sh
 cargo build --release -p horizon-client --bins
 C=target/release/horizon-ctl
 $C launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait   # start the game, open or create the world, wait for it
 $C state                                     # player, world, screen, crosshair target
 $C find-block birch_log                      # the 16 nearest loaded logs
 $C goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5              # walk there along a path
 $C break -1 65 -3                            # mine it: {"drops": {"minecraft:birch_log": 1}, ...}
 $C inventory                                 # hotbar, inventory, armor, offhand, counts
 $C open-inventory                            # craft planks in the 2x2 grid:
 $C click-slot 0; $C click-slot 100 right; $C click-slot 0; $C click-slot 200 shift; $C close
 $C place 2 65 -2 --item birch_planks         # {"changed": true, "block": {...}}
 $C pause; $C ui                              # the pause menu's widgets: ids, kinds, labels, bounds
 $C click options; $C set fov 0.75; $C click done   # widgets by id
 $C screenshot /tmp/view.png                  # PNG of the next presented frame
 $C quit                                      # save and exit
 ```
 
 `horizon-ctl help` lists the commands by group and `horizon-ctl COMMAND --help`
 explains one with examples; `horizon-ctl help --game` lists what the running
 game accepts, test hooks included.
 
 - **Observe:** `state` (position, rotation, velocity, health, food, saturation,
   XP, effects, game mode, dimension, time, weather, the screen and what the
   crosshair points at), `looking-at`, `entities [RADIUS] [TYPE]` (mobs with
   ids and health, dropped items, orbs), `block X Y Z`, `blocks X1 Y1 Z1 X2 Y2 Z2`, `light X1 Y1 Z1 X2 Y2 Z2`,
   `find-block BLOCK [RADIUS]`, `inventory` (stacks with their components as
   SNBT), `screen` (the open screen or title menu, its buttons and slots) and
   `messages` (chat, title, subtitle and action bar).
 - **Move and act:** `move DIR SECONDS`, `jump`, `goto X Y Z` (A* over standable
   blocks: steps up one block, drops up to three, avoids lava), `look`,
   `look-at` a point, block face or entity, `attack [ID]`, `break X Y Z`,
   `place X Y Z [--item ITEM]`, `interact X Y Z` (doors, chests, crafting
   tables), `use-item [--hold S]` (eat, drink, throw), `select SLOT|ITEM`, `drop`.

**Investigating compilation issues**

Compiling could take a while, and I might not need to edit anything just yet. I’m pondering whether to investigate the baseline using the session store, but maybe that’s not necessary. There’s an issue with the source code using `std::env::current_dir()?.join`, which complicates things. 

In the Android environment, the gamepad feature `gilrs` compiles but doesn’t support any controller backend. Even though cargo checks out, there’s no input runtime for controllers, and it may need some explicit noting later. Also, I'm checking on the audio support with `cpal` and discovered that it might work with Android's Oboe backend. I see `winit` is set for the Android clone, but the telemetry seems absent on Android. Fullscreen mode is not yet addressed.

**Exploring Android development details**

In native Android, I'm noticing it uses actual graphics instance descriptor backends with `.with_env()`, which automatically includes Vulkan and OpenGL. The app can support OpenGL if Vulkan isn't available, which is good. 

The device resumed handling is managed by winit. I'm curious about the clipboard JNI code obtaining the app's Android context. It looks like it’s set by an event loop, but I need to check if the initialization happens correctly. There’s also a resource issue with screen pixel text using many vertices during redrawing, and I need to update comments regarding the `game_home` config branch.

 # Horizon Android builds
 
 This project contains two separate ARM64 NativeActivity APKs: the known-good Vulkan render check and an early APK wired to Horizon's actual Rust client.
 
 The render-check APK is only a diagnostic; it does not load a world or use the game's renderer. The client APK launches `horizon-client` through its existing `winit` event loop and `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`. Neither APK bundles Minecraft resources or server JARs. PojavLauncher is not used.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 - Android starts `android.app.NativeActivity` from `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`; its library name is `horizon_android`.
 - `android/native` builds the render-check library; `android/client-native` builds the game library. Their separate Gradle modules, native library names, and application IDs keep the smoke-test APK independently buildable and installable.
 - The client APK's `android_main(AndroidApp)` initializes Android logging and calls `horizon_client::run_android`. The client stores files in its app-specific external files directory; Android's activity lifecycle, surface, and input are forwarded by winit.
 - winit receives the `AndroidApp` through `EventLoopBuilderExtAndroid::with_android_app`. Its resumed/suspended/window events create and release the probe surface/renderer.
 - The smoke check is Vulkan-only. The game retains its existing renderer and graphics-backend selection.
 - The diagnostic uses the same pinned winit and wgpu versions as Horizon. It is intentionally separate from `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`.
 
 ## Build the debug APK on Linux x86-64
 
 Toolchain baseline: Rust 1.95.0, JDK 17, Gradle 8.13, Android Gradle Plugin 8.7.2, SDK Platform/Build Tools 35, and NDK 27.2.12479018. Rust 1.95.0 is required by the current Horizon workspace (`horizon-mods`); it is newer than the standalone probe's original Rust baseline.
 
 Install the Android Rust target once:
 
 ```sh
 rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --profile minimal
 rustup target add aarch64-linux-android --toolchain 1.95.0
 ```
 
 Set the Android/JDK environment and build:
 
 ```sh
 export JAVA_HOME="$HOME/.local/jdks/temurin-17.0.13+11"
 export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android/Sdk"
 export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_HOME"
 export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/27.2.12479018"
 export ANDROID_NDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_NDK_HOME"
 export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
 
 sdkmanager --licenses
 sdkmanager --install "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "ndk;27.2.12479018"
 
 cd horizon/android
 ./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace :app:assembleDebug :clientApp:assembleDebug
 ```
 
 Gradle runs the pinned Rust toolchain for `aarch64-linux-android`, uses the NDK's API-26 linker, and copies each native library into that module's generated build output before packaging.
 
 The standalone render-check APK is:
 
 ```text
 horizon/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
 ```
 
 The actual-client APK is:
 
 ```text
 horizon/android/clientApp/build/outputs/apk/debug/clientApp-debug.apk
 ```
 
 The client uses Horizon's existing `fast` Rust profile to avoid the high memory cost of release LTO when compiling the large client crate.
 
 ## Install and test on a physical Android device (Windows PowerShell)
 
 Use an arm64 device with Android API 26+ and Vulkan 1.0 support. From the repository root, install and launch:
 
 ```powershell
 $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
 $apk = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\android\clientApp\build\outputs\apk\debug\clientApp-debug.apk).Path
 adb devices -l
 adb install -r $apk
 adb shell am force-stop dev.playhorizon.horizon.client
 adb logcat -c
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon.client/android.app.NativeActivity
 adb logcat -v threadtime -s HorizonClient:I AndroidRuntime:E
 ```
 
 Without resources the client should present a resource-setup screen; this proves client startup and rendering only, not gameplay. Prepare resources on a PC from your own licensed Minecraft installation and your own 26.3 server JAR, following [the resource preparation instructions](../docs/native-client.md#run-from-a-checkout). Do not copy the server JAR itself. From the repository root, copy the prepared directory to the app-specific files folder:
 
 ```powershell
 $prepared = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\.local\horizon-client\26.3).Path
 $destination = '/sdcard/Android/data/dev.playhorizon.horizon.client/files/resources'
 adb shell "mkdir -p $destination"
 adb push $prepared $destination
 adb shell am force-stop dev.playhorizon.horizon.client
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon.client/android.app.NativeActivity
 adb logcat -v threadtime -s HorizonClient:I AndroidRuntime:E
 ```
 
 After import, look for `Horizon: resources loaded` and the title screen. Entering a local world must be tested separately before claiming gameplay works. Audio output, touch controls, gamepad input, suspend/resume, and real-device gameplay have not yet been validated.
 
 To retest the separate diagnostic APK:
 
 ```powershell
 $apk = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\android\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk).Path
 adb install -r $apk
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon/android.app.NativeActivity
 adb logcat -d -v threadtime -s HorizonAndroid:I AndroidRuntime:E |
     Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-render.log
 @(
     "manufacturer=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer)"
     "model=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.model)"
     "android=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.release)"
     "api=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.sdk)"
     "abi=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abi)"
 ) | Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-device.txt
 adb shell screencap -p /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png
 adb pull /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png .\horizon-android-render.png
 ```
 
 A successful smoke render must show the diagnostic frame and matching `PRESENTED_FRAME` evidence identifying the Vulkan backend, adapter, dimensions, and format. For the client, the `ANDROID_CLIENT start` log, rendered resource-setup screen, rendered title screen after import, and successful world entry are separate checkpoints. APK compilation or Activity launch alone proves none of the later checkpoints.
 
 The APK output above is separate from `/workspaces/horizon-android/app-debug.apk`, the already-tested standalone probe APK; this build does not overwrite that file.
 
 ## Current limitations
 
 - The Android clipboard path uses the Android clipboard manager; physical clipboard behavior is unverified.
 - Android controller input and DualSense HID output are not yet supported by Horizon's current `gilrs` backend. Android builds a logged no-HID-output stub for DualSense.
 - Touchscreen controls, audio behavior, suspend/resume, resource import through a file picker, and actual local-world gameplay are not yet validated.
 - A prior standalone rendering probe ran on a Xiaomi Redmi Note 13, but neither APK's latest build has been tested on that device.

diff --git a/workspaces/horizon-android/horizon/android/README.md b/workspaces/horizon-android/horizon/android/README.md

--- a/workspaces/horizon-android/horizon/android/README.md
+++ b/workspaces/horizon-android/horizon/android/README.md
@@ -1,220 +1,220 @@
 # Horizon Android builds
 
 This project contains two separate ARM64 NativeActivity APKs: the known-good Vulkan render check and an early APK wired to Horizon's actual Rust client.
 
 The render-check APK is only a diagnostic; it does not load a world or use the game's renderer. The client APK launches `horizon-client` through its existing `winit` event loop and `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`. Neither APK bundles Minecraft resources or server JARs. PojavLauncher is not used.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 - Android starts `android.app.NativeActivity` from `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`; its library name is `horizon_android`.
 - `android/native` builds the render-check library; `android/client-native` builds the game library. Their separate Gradle modules, native library names, and application IDs keep the smoke-test APK independently buildable and installable.
 - The client APK's `android_main(AndroidApp)` initializes Android logging and calls `horizon_client::run_android`. The client stores files in its app-specific external files directory; Android's activity lifecycle, surface, and input are forwarded by winit.
 - winit receives the `AndroidApp` through `EventLoopBuilderExtAndroid::with_android_app`. Its resumed/suspended/window events drive the client window and existing renderer.
 - The smoke check is Vulkan-only. The game retains its existing renderer and graphics-backend selection.
 - The diagnostic uses the same pinned winit and wgpu versions as Horizon. It is intentionally separate from `horizon-client::gfx::Renderer`.
 
 ## Build the debug APK on Linux x86-64
 
 Toolchain baseline: Rust 1.95.0, JDK 17, Gradle 8.13, Android Gradle Plugin 8.7.2, SDK Platform/Build Tools 35, and NDK 27.2.12479018. Rust 1.95.0 is required by the current Horizon workspace (`horizon-mods`); it is newer than the standalone probe's original Rust baseline.
 
 Install the Android Rust target once:
 
 ```sh
 rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --profile minimal
 rustup target add aarch64-linux-android --toolchain 1.95.0
 ```
 
 Set the Android/JDK environment and build:
 
 ```sh
 export JAVA_HOME="$HOME/.local/jdks/temurin-17.0.13+11"
 export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android/Sdk"
 export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_HOME"
 export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/27.2.12479018"
 export ANDROID_NDK_ROOT="$ANDROID_NDK_HOME"
 export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
 
 sdkmanager --licenses
 sdkmanager --install "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "ndk;27.2.12479018"
 
 cd horizon/android
 ./gradlew --no-daemon --stacktrace :app:assembleDebug :clientApp:assembleDebug
 ```
 
 Gradle runs the pinned Rust toolchain for `aarch64-linux-android`, uses the NDK's API-26 linker, and copies each native library into that module's generated build output before packaging.
 
 The standalone render-check APK is:
 
 ```text
 horizon/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
 ```
 
 The actual-client APK is:
 
 ```text
 horizon/android/clientApp/build/outputs/apk/debug/clientApp-debug.apk
 ```
 
 The client uses Horizon's existing `fast` Rust profile to avoid the high memory cost of release LTO when compiling the large client crate.
 
 ## Install and test on a physical Android device (Windows PowerShell)
 
 Use an arm64 device with Android API 26+ and Vulkan 1.0 support. From the repository root, install and launch:
 
 ```powershell
 $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
 $apk = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\android\clientApp\build\outputs\apk\debug\clientApp-debug.apk).Path
 adb devices -l
 adb install -r $apk
 adb shell am force-stop dev.playhorizon.horizon.client
 adb logcat -c
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon.client/android.app.NativeActivity
 adb logcat -v threadtime -s HorizonClient:I AndroidRuntime:E
 ```
 
 Without resources the client should present a resource-setup screen; this proves client startup and rendering only, not gameplay. Prepare resources on a PC from your own licensed Minecraft installation and your own 26.3 server JAR, following [the resource preparation instructions](../docs/native-client.md#run-from-a-checkout). Do not copy the server JAR itself. From the repository root, copy the prepared directory to the app-specific files folder:
 
 ```powershell
 $prepared = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\.local\horizon-client\26.3).Path
 $destination = '/sdcard/Android/data/dev.playhorizon.horizon.client/files/resources'
 adb shell "mkdir -p $destination"
 adb push $prepared $destination
 adb shell am force-stop dev.playhorizon.horizon.client
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon.client/android.app.NativeActivity
 adb logcat -v threadtime -s HorizonClient:I AndroidRuntime:E
 ```
 
 After import, look for `Horizon: resources loaded` and the title screen. Entering a local world must be tested separately before claiming gameplay works. Audio output, touch controls, gamepad input, suspend/resume, and real-device gameplay have not yet been validated.
 
 To retest the separate diagnostic APK:
 
 ```powershell
 $apk = (Resolve-Path .\horizon\android\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk).Path
 adb install -r $apk
 adb shell am start -n dev.playhorizon.horizon/android.app.NativeActivity
 adb logcat -d -v threadtime -s HorizonAndroid:I AndroidRuntime:E |
     Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-render.log
 @(
     "manufacturer=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.manufacturer)"
     "model=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.model)"
     "android=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.release)"
     "api=$(adb shell getprop ro.build.version.sdk)"
     "abi=$(adb shell getprop ro.product.cpu.abi)"
 ) | Tee-Object -FilePath .\horizon-android-device.txt
 adb shell screencap -p /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png
 adb pull /sdcard/horizon-android-render.png .\horizon-android-render.png
 ```
 
 A successful smoke render must show the diagnostic frame and matching `PRESENTED_FRAME` evidence identifying the Vulkan backend, adapter, dimensions, and format. For the client, the `ANDROID_CLIENT start` log, rendered resource-setup screen, rendered title screen after import, and successful world entry are separate checkpoints. APK compilation or Activity launch alone proves none of the later checkpoints.
 
 The APK output above is separate from `/workspaces/horizon-android/app-debug.apk`, the already-tested standalone probe APK; this build does not overwrite that file.
 
 ## Current limitations
 
 - The Android clipboard path uses the Android clipboard manager; physical clipboard behavior is unverified.
 - Android controller input and DualSense HID output are not yet supported by Horizon's current `gilrs` backend. Android builds a logged no-HID-output stub for DualSense.
 - Touchscreen controls, audio behavior, suspend/resume, resource import through a file picker, and actual local-world gameplay are not yet validated.
 - A prior standalone rendering probe ran on a Xiaomi Redmi Note 13, but neither APK's latest build has been tested on that device.
